fields.quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.
fields.note: The listed unlawful acts, the written notice requirement, the posting of the notice and Rent Board administration of complaints are all in the document.

fields.quoted_span: Any landlord found to be in violation of the Ordinance shall be subject to administrative fines of at least $1,000 and up to $10,000 per violation, civil damages including actual damages or three times the amount of one month's rent, punitive damages, attorneys' fees and costs, and injunctive relief.

fields.note: The record's effective date is null. The document gives only the April 14, 2020 passage date and no effective date.

fields.quoted_span: The City of Berkeley Rent Stabilization Board will be administering complaints regarding the Ordinance.
fields.note: The page describes current administration and enforcement, which implies the ordinance is in force. It never states in so many words that the ordinance is in force.

fields.quoted_span: Owner-occupied properties (between 1-3 units) in which an owner of record resides in one of the units as their primary residence
fields.note: The other listed exemptions (lifetime sex offenders, limited public housing/Section 8 exemptions, BMC 13.76.130 A.9 move-back units, sublet/roommate units) are also in the document. Coverage of current and prospective tenants matches the document. The exemption requirements are not detailed, consistent with the requires_unknown_facts flag.

fields.quoted_span: On April 14, 2020, Berkeley City Council passed the Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance (BMC 13.106).
fields.note: The page also lists 'Municipal Code 13.106' as related BMC.
